one_liner: Single-header SIMD BC1 (DXT1) block encoder from NVTT; at the highest quality levels it is faster than RGBCX only when built with AVX2 or AVX-512.
what_it_does: ICBC compresses one 4x4 block of float RGBA (0..1) plus per-texel weights into an 8-byte BC1 block, at one of ten quality levels. It can optionally use 3-colour mode and encode black texels as transparent black. The caller does image blocking, threading and file output. The API is icbc::init(decoder) once, then compress_bc1(level, colors, weights, color_weights, three_color_mode, three_color_black, out), plus decode_bc1 and evaluate_bc1_error helpers. The encoder can be tuned to the D3D10, NVIDIA, AMD or Intel hardware decoder's palette rounding. It is BC1 only: compress_bc3 is declared but is a stub.
how_it_is_fast: The quality ladder runs from bounding-box fit (level 0) through box fit plus least-squares endpoints (level 1) to squish-style cluster fit over every order-preserving 4-cluster partition (968 combinations) and 3-cluster partition (152), with 3-colour mode at levels 8 and 9 and iterative endpoint refinement at level 9. Near-duplicate colours are merged first, under a per-level threshold, to cut the combination count. Each partition's least-squares error comes from summed-area tables, as in rgbcx, and the cluster-fit loop is vectorised over 4/8/16 lanes. The SIMD back end (SSE2, SSE4.1, AVX, AVX2, AVX-512, NEON, AltiVec) is chosen at compile time, and the AVX2 and AVX-512 paths use permute instructions for table lookups. The SIMD path does most of the work: in doc/results.txt the AVX-512 build is about 9x faster than the scalar build on Sky Lake (0.166 s vs 1.519 s), with identical PSNR.
when_to_use: Offline or build-pipeline BC1 compression where you want the top quality band (above about 30.7 dB average on the author's Kodim+Waterloo chart). There the AVX-512 build reaches RGBCX's best quality in roughly a quarter of the time.
x86-64 build machines where you can compile a dedicated AVX2 or AVX-512 binary. The scalar build is slower than RGBCX at almost every quality level on the same chart.
Texture tools that already use NVTT, or that need BC1 tuned to a specific GPU vendor's decoder rounding (D3D10, NVIDIA, AMD/Apple M1, Intel).
Embedding with no build system: one MIT header with no dependencies beyond the C/C++ standard headers and SIMD intrinsics.
when_not_to_use: Low and mid quality BC1. In the chart, stb_dxt and RGBCX's lowest levels match ICBC below about 30.1 dB, and RGBCX (about 30.52 dB at about 0.5 time units) beats the AVX-512 ICBC points at about 30.38 and 30.57 dB (about 0.75 each). For real-time encoding, Goofy is far faster at much lower quality.
Anything beyond BC1 (BC3/4/5/7): compress_bc3 returns 0 and writes nothing, and the alpha/BC4/BC5 encoders are open issue #3. The README itself recommends RGBCX as the better-supported library.

Shipping one portable x86 binary: there is no runtime CPU dispatch, so an AVX-512 or AVX2 build faults on CPUs without those instructions, and a portable build falls back to the slow SSE2 or scalar path.
PowerPC: according to open PR #10 (August 2026), the AltiVec/VMX back end never compiled, with typos, missing mask/any/all functions and a wrong vec_div.
Teams that need maintenance: the last commit was 2022-11-09, and PR #10 and 6 issues are open with no maintainer response.

integration.form: header-only (define ICBC_IMPLEMENTATION in one translation unit)
integration.dependencies: none (standard C headers plus x86/ARM/PowerPC intrinsics headers); the test harness adds stb_image, stb_image_write and ic_pfor.h
integration.min_toolchain: C++11 (icbc_test.cpp's compile comment reads 'g++ icbc_test.cpp -O3 -mavx2 -lpthread -std=c+=11', a typo for c++11; build.bat uses MSVC 2019 'cl /O2 /arch:AVX512'; results.txt runs used MSVC 2017/2019, clang 11/13 and gcc 8.3/10)
integration.platforms: x86/x86-64 (SSE2 to AVX-512, selected at compile time from __AVX512F__/__AVX2__/__AVX__/__SSE4_1__ or ICBC_SIMD), ARM NEON, scalar fallback; the PowerPC VMX path is broken
integration.thread_safety: Call icbc::init() once before encoding: it fills global lookup tables and the default decoder. compress_bc1 then reads only those tables, and icbc_test.cpp calls it from all threads at once through ic_pfor.

gotchas: Encoding before icbc::init() leaves the single-colour and cluster tables zeroed. The decoder passed to init changes the produced blocks, so encode for the decoder you ship on.
Automatic NEON selection checks only __ARM_NEON__. Compilers that define only the ACLE macro __ARM_NEON (GCC for AArch64, for example) may silently fall back to scalar unless ICBC_SIMD is set to -1.

three_color_black=true (used in the chart for ICBC and RGBCX) stores black texels with the transparent-black index. That raises PSNR but makes those texels alpha 0 when the texture is sampled as RGBA.
Input is 16 float RGBA texels per block, not 8-bit pixels. Conversion, edge padding and block layout are the caller's job, and the test harness rounds image sizes down to multiples of 4.
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick ICBC over rgbcx in bc7enc only when you need the highest-quality BC1 on AVX2/AVX-512 build machines and can live with an unmaintained, BC1-only header. Otherwise rgbcx (also BC3-5, faster in the mid-quality range) is the default, and Goofy is the choice for real-time speed at a large quality loss.
verified_claims_summary: The only comparison is the author's chart of average PSNR on the Kodim and Waterloo sets against encode time, with an unlabelled time unit, made with ICBC 1.03 (current header 1.05), RGBCX 1.12, a modified stb_dxt 1.09, squish 1.15 and AMD CMP_Core. At the top quality (about 30.9 dB), ICBC-AVX512 takes about 5.5 units against about 20.6 for scalar RGBCX; ICBC-Scalar is slower than RGBCX at most levels, so the lead is SIMD rather than the algorithm. The repo's harness (icbc_test.cpp) times only ICBC, on the 24 Kodak images alone, multithreaded through ic_pfor, so the chart's baseline timings, threading and machine cannot be reproduced from public code. Since v1.03, commits from September 2022 changed low-quality inset handling and added level 0, so the chart's curve no longer describes the current code. Third-party data in Goofy's README (i7-7820HQ, one thread) measured the older icbc v1.0 SSE2 at 24 MP/s and 41.00 dB, against rgbcx 1.08 level 0 at 60 MP/s and 40.85 dB and stb_dxt at 43 MP/s and 40.82 dB. No correctness bug was found behind the BC1 numbers.
status_note: Abandoned since 2022-11-09 (157 commits, 131 stars, MIT), though it remains NVTT's BC1 encoder. It is small and dependency-free enough to vendor; build per-ISA binaries and do not rely on the VMX or BC3 entry points.
